NKE.rationale: NKE is a structurally deteriorating business with no visible fundamental inflection. Revenue is flat ($11.28B Q3 FY2026, +0.1% YoY) while profitability is collapsing: EPS down 35.2% YoY to $0.35, operating margin compressed to 5.8% (from 7.5%), net margin at 4.6% (from 9.4% a year ago). Operating cash flow plunged 76% YoY to $430M. The 29.2x P/E is misleading — it reflects depressed earnings, not cheapness; earnings yield of 3.4% sits below the 4.41% risk-free rate. Market share is eroding for the third consecutive year (down ~3pp to 22.9% per Euromonitor). Management has lowered the recovery timeline, delaying gross margin expansion to Q2 2027 and guiding for low-single-digit revenue declines for three more quarters. Short interest has surged to 4.67% of float. The EEOC DEI investigation, 14,000 layoffs, and 37% of assortment sold at discount signal a business in genuine structural distress. The stock's -29.2% quarterly decline and -32% YTD are directionally consistent with fundamentals, not an overshoot. No near-term catalyst exists to re-rate the stock; the earliest margin recovery is Q2 2027. All three pillars — deteriorating fundamentals, no valuation support (earnings yield below risk-free), and absence of a near-term re-rating catalyst — align negatively.
